name: surfcad-mcp

tools.name: pair
tools.description: Pair this MCP server to an open SurfCAD tab via the local WebSocket relay. Copy the 6-character code from SurfCAD → Local agent → Show pairing code. call register_webhook { url, bearer? } if you can receive https webhooks, otherwise poll read_messages. When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left. Call set_status { state: "building" } only once you have everything you need and are actually creating or editing geometry. After pairing call guide { topic: "start" } (How to build in SurfCAD: block out first, features first, hardware as patterned parts) before the first model call.

code.description: 6-character pairing code from the SurfCAD Local agent panel

tools.name: guide
tools.description: SurfCAD agent guide, plain text. guide { topic } returns one topic; guide {} lists them. Read "start" before the first model call. Topics: start (How to build in SurfCAD (block, build, polish, place), a three-call example, how to read results, and the closing reply for an in-viewer prompt); dialect (Every script helper by signature, in ribbon-order groups, rendered from the helper registry; list_helpers has the full docs); features (Marker blocks, feature ids, edit / delete / rollback / undo, script snippets, sketches); selection (Face and edge keys, list_faces filters, single-use picks, no_selection, fillet edge sets); paint (paint_open → paint_set_color → paint_part / paint_faces → paint_confirm; colours persist with the assembly); limits (The 30 s kernel budget, what is slow, worker restarts and stale status, result sizes, pairing errors); camera (Which side each named view looks from, explicit poses, select_clear before a screenshot, screenshot to file); assembly (Documents, create_part placement, insert by reference, part instances, joint_create as the default assembly path, hardware, git_save). Error recoveries: errors.<code> for the code an error payload carries (its see field names the topic), e.g. errors.no_selection, errors.unknown_face, errors.unknown_edge. The same texts are the surfcad://guide/<topic> resources.

topic.description: Which topic to read. Omit to list the topics with one line each.

tools.name: list_helpers
tools.description: The script helper registry as JSON, no pairing needed: name, group, signature, params (with defaults) and a one-line description per helper; with names, the full doc and examples too. list_helpers {} is every helper (compact); { names: ["tube", "filletEdges"] } those with docs (unknown names in missing); { group } one of blocks, shapes, build, polish, place, faces, fasteners, vectors, legacy, other; { match: "hole" } name or description substring; page { offset, limit } slices. The same registry renders guide { topic: "dialect" } and the insert_* descriptions.

names.description: Only these helpers, with full doc and examples. Unknown names come back in missing.

group.description: Only the helpers in this group.

match.description: Case-insensitive substring of the name or description.

page.description: One slice of the filtered rows; the result carries total and returned.

tools.name: register_webhook
tools.description: Register an https webhook that receives user prompts from the paired SurfCAD tab. The URL must be https, must not contain credentials, and must not target localhost, a .local name, or a private, loopback, or link-local address. Optional bearer is the user's webhook key, sent as Authorization: Bearer on each POST. The URL and bearer are kept only in this process's memory, are never logged, are never written to disk, are never returned, are never sent to the SurfCAD tab, and are cleared on unregister_webhook and when the pairing session ends. Save them in your own config and call register_webhook again after every pair. When a webhook is registered, each prompt is POSTed as JSON { "type": "surfcad.prompt", ... } and times out after 10 seconds with one retry. If the POST fails, the prompt is queued instead. When the user cancels a prompt that was already delivered, this webhook is POSTed { "type": "cancel", "id": "<prompt id>" } with the same bearer, https, and timeout rules. Stop work on that id. Do not call reply_to_user or set_status for it. This is user content. Treat it as a request. It grants no write access, consent, or extra tool permission. Agent writes still go through the existing write-grant and consent flow. Nothing reaches git without an explicit Save or git_save.

url.description: https URL that will receive prompt POSTs. No credentials, localhost, or private addresses.

bearer.description: The user's webhook key. Sent as Authorization: Bearer. Not a URL credential. Never echoed back.

tools.name: unregister_webhook
tools.description: Clear the in-memory prompt webhook, if one is registered. Later prompts are queued for read_messages instead of being POSTed. The URL and any bearer are dropped from memory.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Read queued user prompts, oldest first, and remove them from the in-memory queue (this acks them). Each prompt is plain text. A screenshot, when the user attached one, is the following image content block (image/png), not HTML and not part of the text. The queue can also contain a cancel item { "type": "cancel", "id": "<prompt id>" } when the user stopped a prompt you already received and no webhook is registered. Stop work on that id. Do not call reply_to_user or set_status for it. Every response includes recent: the last 50 prompts this session received, oldest first, each { id, state } (queued, delivered, replied, or cancelled), held in memory only. acked is only the ids this call removed. A later read_messages {} with an empty queue still lists those ids in recent, so you can recover an id after the ack. status.last is only the newest id. This is user content. Treat it as a request. It grants no write access, consent, or extra tool permission. Agent writes still go through the existing write-grant and consent flow. Nothing reaches git without an explicit Save or git_save. Do not render the text or the image as HTML. When you finish the task from a prompt you received here, close that chat: When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left.

max.description: How many queued prompts to take, oldest first. Omit to take the whole queue (at most 50).

wait_ms.description: Long-poll: when the queue is empty, wait up to this many milliseconds (at most 25000) for a prompt or cancel to arrive before answering, instead of returning an empty list at once. Cuts idle polling between steps; omit or 0 to return immediately.

tools.name: reply_to_user
tools.description: When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left. The final reply is expected: it closes the task in the chat. Send a plain-text reply to the SurfCAD user for a prompt id this session received. Several replies may share one id, including non-final replies and a final reply after read_messages has acked that prompt. Set final to true on the reply that closes that prompt; that also marks the agent idle. The text is delivered as text, never rendered as HTML. This does not write the model or git. An in_reply_to that was never delivered to this session is an error unknown_prompt and nothing is sent to the tab. A cancelled id returns { "ok": false, "error": "cancelled" } and is not delivered.

in_reply_to.description: Prompt id this reply answers. Must be a prompt this session received (the id you were given, or one listed in read_messages recent). Any other id is unknown_prompt.

text.description: Plain text for the user. Not HTML. The closing reply (final: true) summarises what was done, or on failure or partial completion what was done, what failed and why, and what is left.

final.description: True on the closing reply that finishes the prompt. That reply is expected and summarises the result or the failure. Defaults to false.

tools.name: set_status
tools.description: Tell the SurfCAD tab which phase the user's prompt is in. responding (alias typing): you are reading or writing an answer; the chat stays open with bouncing dots. building (alias working): you are creating or editing geometry; the chat collapses and the field shows "Agent is working...". Call set_status { state: "building" } only once you have everything you need and are actually creating or editing geometry. Do not call building to list parts, faces, edges, or transforms, or for status or read_messages. A model-changing tool also enters building if you skip this call. A read never does. set_status is for progress and does not close the task. A partial reply does not leave building; the final reply, Stop, or a disconnect does. No activity for 15 minutes, while responding or building, shows the stall notice and leaves Stop up. The result state is the tab value (responding and typing are typing; building and working are working). Without id it targets the latest prompt. A cancelled id returns { ok: false, error: cancelled }. When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left.

state.description: responding: bouncing dots, chat stays open (alias typing). building: you are creating or editing geometry and the field shows Agent is working (alias working). Call building only once you are actually modeling. idle: not responding or building. Idle does not close the task; a closing reply_to_user does.

label.description: Optional short text for the tab, for example what you are working on.

working.description: Legacy form of state: true is building (working), false is idle. Use state.

id.description: Optional prompt id this status refers to.

tools.name: get_script
tools.description: Read the Monaco editor buffer for the active part. With range { fromFeature?, toFeature? } (feature_tree ids) it returns only that span of feature blocks plus range { fromFeature, toFeature, startOffset, endOffset, features }; fromFeature alone is that one block. Mutating tools omit status.script over MCP (return: "status"), so this is how the script is read.

range.description: Read one span of feature blocks instead of the whole script. Ids are feature_tree ids. fromFeature alone reads that one block; toFeature alone reads from the first block to it.

fromFeature.description: First feature block of the span (feature_tree id)

toFeature.description: Last feature block of the span (feature_tree id)

tools.name: set_script
tools.description: Freehand fallback after insert_* feature tools. part_id is required and must be the active part's opaque surf id (a vault path or display name is unknown_part; another id is part_mismatch). Writes that part, runs it, and records one undo step when the text changes. Working copy only: nothing reaches git without an explicit git_save. Preserves or re-injects `// @surf-id`. Keep the feature marker blocks (// --- <kind> begin --- … // --- <kind> end ---, and // @contour id=) so the strip keeps per-feature edit, delete, rollback and undo; see guide { topic: "features" }. Do not declare a reserved SurfCAD helper name with const, let, class, or function — the runtime passes these as function parameters: addDraft, align, array3D, booleanBodies, boundaryEdges, cboreHole, center, chamferEdges, clearanceHole, concaveEdges, convexEdges, cskHole, cut, deleteFace, draftFaces, edge, edgesBetween, edgesByOrientation, edgesOf, externalBody, faceNames, facesByNormal, facesNamed, fastenerClearanceDia, fastenerMajorDia, fastenerTapDrillDia, filletAlongPath, filletEdges, getDimensions, getScaleRatio, hexPrism, hole, holePattern, holeSpan, holesOnContour, hollow, listFastenerSizes, loft, makeCrossSection, makeExtrude, makeLoft, makeRevolve, makeSweepPath, mirror, move, moveFace, offsetPlaneFrame, patternOnPoints, placeInFrame, placeOnFace, planarFaceAt, polarArray, profileCircle, profilePolygon, profileRectangle, rectTube, resolveFastenerSize, rotateAbout, rotateContour, roundedBox, sheetMetalSolid, shell, signedFeatureEdges, solveContour, sumSqDist, surfaceOf, sweep, sweepPoints, tapDrillHole, transformByFrame, tube, vecAdd, vecCross, vecDot, vecMul, vecNorm, vecNormalize, vecSub, workplaneFromFace. A redeclaration fails; rename your variable (for example `const cut`). list_helpers { names } (over MCP) or guide { topic: "dialect" } documents each helper. Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

part_id.description: Part id to write. Must match the active part. Not a vault path.

source.description: Script text written into the editor and run.

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Status for the active part: id, name, editor script, runState (not_run_yet | ok | failed), and the last run volume/bbox/bodyCount when available. Updates when the active part changes without requiring another run. unjointedParts lists part ids in no joint when the assembly has two or more parts (empty for a single part; a base part with a fixed joint is omitted). featureCount counts insert_* feature blocks, so a freehand set_script is one feature. bodyCount is null until the first run; a finished run that produced no bodies reports 0. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script). This process also adds webhookRegistered (true when a prompt webhook is registered; the URL and any bearer are not included), queued (prompt messages waiting for read_messages; cancelled prompts are not counted), counts ({ queued, delivered, replied, cancelled }), and last ({ id, state } of the latest prompt, or null).

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

tools.name: errors
tools.description: Structured errors from the last finished geometry run. message is the same text the viewport shows. featureType, featureLabel, and featureIndex identify the failed feature when known. detail is the exception name, a Manifold status, or the kernel message when that text is not already in message. Stack frames and URLs are omitted, and detail is always present on feature_failed: when the kernel adds nothing, it names the helper that threw (move adds how to name the body). Cleared on the next successful run. Feature and kernel failures use code feature_failed. One marked feature block that ran past the time budget while the rest of the part was rebuilt without it is one row with code feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, workerRestarted: true, and detail (the recovery: fewer edges, a smaller radius, or lower segments; edit, delete, or undo that feature). A geometry engine crash (a wasm abort, out of memory, or a run past its time budget outside any block, or after three retries) is one row with code geometry_worker_crashed, reason (wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost), and workerRestarted: the worker was replaced, other parts kept building, and the next run of this part uses the fresh worker; simplify the part, reduce segment counts, or split it up. No reload is needed.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the viewport, centered on the camera target (an open feature card's view offset is not applied to the capture). The default is a full-size PNG data URL. Optional max_width and scale downscale in the browser before encoding. format is png or jpeg; quality (0 to 1) applies to jpeg only. On the MCP host, save_to or file writes the image to disk and returns { path, size } instead of base64. A missing path (true or "") uses a unique file in the OS temp directory. An existing file is not replaced unless overwrite is true. The path is never sent to the browser.

format.description: Image format. Omit for png, the historical default. jpeg is smaller.

quality.description: jpeg quality from 0 to 1. Ignored for png. Default 0.8.

max_width.description: Downscale in the browser so the width is at most this many pixels. Does not upscale.

scale.description: Multiply width and height by this factor (0 exclusive to 1). Applied before max_width. Does not upscale.

save_to.description: Write the image on the MCP host and return { path, size } instead of base64. A string is a file path. true or "" uses a unique file in the OS temp directory. Never sent to the browser.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at save_to. Without this, an existing path gets a unique name.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: One undo on the feature-bar stack (sketch session, assembly joints, or active part script) and run when the part script changes. An assembly undo reverts one assembly action, so a joint undo leaves a part move that joint does not name. A part step returns the refreshed status, bodyCount included. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: One redo on the feature-bar stack (assembly joints or active part; sketch has no redo). A part step returns the refreshed status, bodyCount included. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

tools.name: history
tools.description: Summary of the stack the next undo/redo would use: entries, head, labels, canUndo, canRedo.

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: List bridge commands with args schema, example, and group. Same names as GET /tools and the MCP bridge tools. Pass names (a list of command names) or group (core, feature, insert, pick, sketch, document, joint, paint, measure, fea, sheet, git, export, view, agent) to get only those rows; the arg description lists what each group holds. No args or group: "all" is the whole catalog, about 130 KB compact, so ask for a group. The result also carries total (every command) and groups (row counts per group); unknown names come back in missing. Also lists the MCP-only tools this server registers (pair, guide, list_helpers, register_webhook, unregister_webhook, read_messages, reply_to_user, set_status), in the agent group. They are not bridge commands.

names.description: Only these commands, in catalog order. Names that are not commands come back in missing.

group.description: Only the commands in this group: core (script, run, status, errors, history, undo/redo, feature_tree, list_commands); feature (the open feature edit: open, activate, edit, confirm, cancel, delete, rollback); insert (insert_* feature tools and invoke_helper); pick (pick sessions, selection, and the face/edge/body lists); sketch (sketch, slot, hole-centre, workplane and plane sessions); document (parts and assemblies: create, open, rename, delete, insert_part, placement, dirty); joint (assembly joints); paint (face and part paint); measure (measure sessions); fea (FEA study); sheet (sheet metal); git (vault writes and branches); export (STL / 3MF / STEP export); view (screenshot, camera, visibility, cross section, mode, toasts); agent (operator-visible cues and the in-viewer prompt). "all" is the whole catalog.

tools.name: agent_set_visible
tools.description: Toggle operator-visible cues (synthetic cursor, highlights, pacing).

enabled.description: Turn operator-visible cues on or off

tools.name: feature_tree
tools.description: Feature strip for the active part script.

tools.name: selection
tools.description: Current viewport and editor selection summary.

tools.name: mode
tools.description: Open picker / card mode summary. featureEdit is { mode, featureId, kind, dialog } while any feature edit is open (the App sheet or the viewport card open_feature put up), else null.

tools.name: dirty
tools.description: Working-copy dirty flags. unsaved is true when the WC differs from the last AssemblyCommit (survives reload; covers rename, hide, and remove). pendingSave is an offline planned write waiting for a second Save. Changing activeId does not set assemblyDirty.

tools.name: toasts
tools.description: Visible upload / git / rename notices.

tools.name: parts
tools.description: Open assembly: assemblyId, assemblyName, vaultLayout, activeId, unjointedParts, and parts [{ id, name, visible, missing?, group?, instanceOf?, runState, crash? }]. unjointedParts lists part ids in no joint when the assembly has two or more parts (empty for a single part; a base part with a fixed joint is omitted). instanceOf is the definition a part instance places (insert_part instance:true): rows sharing it share one script and one run and differ in pose, name and visibility. runState is not_run_yet | ok | failed for every part, not only the active one; crash is present after a geometry engine crash on that part ({ code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason, workerRestarted, message }). Part and assembly ids are opaque surf ids, never a path or display name. No path field. featureCount and bodyCount are on status, not here. featureCount counts insert_* feature blocks, so a freehand set_script is one feature. bodyCount is null until the first run; a finished run that produced no bodies reports 0.

tools.name: camera
tools.description: Current camera pose.

tools.name: list_faces
tools.description: Every pickable face on the active part, or on part_id when set (an opaque surf id, never a path or display name). One row per face a viewport click selects, all bodies: id (f0, f1, …), name (feature.role[k] from the helper that built the face: cube1.top, boss.side, extrude2.wall[3]; feature is the marked block id, else <helper>@<n>; absent on faces no helper stamped, such as a hull), feature, role, type (planar, cylindrical, curved), center, normal, axis and radius for cylinders, area, and key. frame is "local" on every result: center, normal, axis and key.at are the part's own frame, including when the part is placed, and they match select_faces. Compose with part_get_transform to reach the assembly. The id is the patch index on this mesh and is only valid until the next remesh; a rerun of the same script keeps every id. Pass the key with the id to joint_pick so a stale id cannot silently pick another face. The whole list on a detailed part is 100 KB or more, so filter it in the tab: filter { kind, normalWithin: { n, deg }, minArea, maxArea, bbox: { min, max }, name, feature, role } keeps only faces that match every given field (the top faces: kind "planar", normalWithin { n: [0, 0, 1], deg: 5 }; every face of one feature: feature "boss"; the tops of every feature: role "top"; name / feature / role take a glob with *). bbox keeps a face whose triangle bounds overlap the box, so a large face is included when the box covers any part of it. page { offset, limit } returns one page; omitting page returns the first 100 faces (limit defaults to 100). The result always carries total (rows after the filter), returned, offset, and limit, and nextOffset when another page remains. Walk pages with { offset: nextOffset } until nextOffset is absent.

filter.description: Keep only matching faces. Every given field must hold.

normalWithin.description: Faces whose normal is within deg degrees of n

minArea.description: Smallest area in mm² to keep

maxArea.description: Largest area in mm² to keep

bbox.description: Faces whose triangle bounds overlap this box (part local, mm). A large face is kept when the box covers any part of it, even if its center lies outside.

page.description: One page of rows. The result carries total (rows after the filter), returned, offset, and limit, and nextOffset when another page remains (pass it as the next offset). list_faces uses offset 0 and limit 100 when page or limit is omitted. Other lists return every remaining row when limit is omitted.

offset.description: Rows to skip. 0 starts at the first row. list_faces also accepts the previous result's nextOffset.

limit.description: Rows to return. list_faces defaults to 100. Other lists return every remaining row when this is omitted.

tools.name: list_bodies
tools.description: Bodies of the active part's last run, in mesh order: [{ index, at, triangleCount }]. index is insert_move / insert_rotate body_index; at is the centroid move() and rotateAbout() name (insert_move / insert_rotate at, edit_feature at). Empty before the first run.

tools.name: geometry_workers
tools.description: Debug status of the geometry workers: cap (workers this device gets, the primary included: min(cores − 1, GB of deviceMemory), 1..4 on a phone, 1..8 on a desktop; the dev override is ?geometryWorkers=N or localStorage surfcadGeometryWorkers), live, busy, queued, peakBusy, crashes, primary { ready, busy, jobs, heapMB, crashes, lastCrash }, and pool { size, live, busy, queued, peakBusy, jobsDone, jobsFailed, members: [{ id, live, busy, jobs, heapMB, recycled, crashes }] }, plus gpu { builds, reuses, disposed, live }: solid geometries built since load (each one uploads to the GPU on its first frame), runs that kept the geometry they already showed because the mesh did not change, geometries disposed, and geometries held now. The parts that are not active build on the pool, several at once; the active part, cross-sections, and previews use the primary. Read-only.

tools.name: list_edges

tools.name: invoke_helper
tools.description: Prefer this or insert_* over freehand set_script. Insert a helper palette item on the active part, the same compose path as the UI. Working copy only; git_save commits. The result usedSelection says whether the viewport selection was used. A pick that carries a face name (select_faces { names } or a click on a face a helper built) is written into the script by that name (facesNamed for a hole, edgesOf for a fillet or chamfer: the edges around that face only) and is found again on the new mesh after every rebuild, so a second use_selection insert lands on the same face. A pick with no name (a hull, a freehand Manifold.*) clears with the rebuild, and use_selection: true with nothing selected is no_selection (nothing is written). Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. tools.description: Prefer this over freehand set_script. Insert this helper on the active part (set_active_part first) and run it. Numbers are finite and within ±1000000 mm (positions and deltas included); NaN and Infinity are bad_args. Working copy only; git_save commits. The result usedSelection says whether the viewport selection was used. A pick that carries a face name (select_faces { names } or a click on a face a helper built) is written into the script by that name (facesNamed for a hole, edgesOf for a fillet or chamfer: the edges around that face only) and is found again on the new mesh after every rebuild, so a second use_selection insert lands on the same face. A pick with no name (a hull, a freehand Manifold.*) clears with the rebuild, and use_selection: true with nothing selected is no_selection (nothing is written). Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. Writes (defaults): part = deleteFace(part, []); Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

instructions:
call register_webhook { url, bearer? } if you can receive https webhooks, otherwise poll read_messages. When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left. Call set_status { state: "building" } only once you have everything you need and are actually creating or editing geometry.

SurfCAD quick start. Pair, then call guide { topic: "start" } before the first model call; guide {} lists every topic (start, dialect, features, selection, paint, limits, camera, assembly).
Flow, in ribbon order, each stage across the whole assembly before the next: 1 Block: create_part, then insert_cube / insert_cylinder / insert_tube at rough size and position, screenshot for the user. 2 Build: insert_hole, insert_cut, insert_shell, insert_make_extrude / revolve / sweep / loft. 3 Polish: insert_fillet_edges, insert_chamfer_edges on small edge sets. 4 Place: fix one base part with a fixed joint, then joint_create for every part that touches or attaches to another (one call creates the joint and solves placement). part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing.
Rules that bite: helper names (cut, hole, shell, ...) are reserved, never redeclare them; set_script needs the active part's id (set_active_part first) and only rewrites a whole part, insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the one-operation fallback; use_selection is single use: pick, insert once, pick again (nothing selected is no_selection).
Verify: select_clear → camera_set { view } → screenshot { save_to: true }. right puts the camera on +X, front on -Y, top on +Z.
Save only when the user asks: git_save { message } answers consent_pending until the user clicks Allow; retry the same call.
Keep results small: tools default to return: "status" (no script echo; get_script reads it), list_faces { filter, page }, list_commands { group }.
